extracted.intended_audience: general public, legal historians, and researchers seeking the text and legal provisions of the English Bill of Rights (1689)
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and interpret the statutory provisions of the English Bill of Rights (1689), which declare rights, limit royal prerogative, and set succession and procedural rules for Parliament and the Crown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegal suspension of laws by regal authority
rubrics_metrics.description: That the pretended power of suspending the laws or the execution of laws by regal authority without consent of Parliament is illegal;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parliament's declaration that a monarch may not suspend statutes or their execution unilaterally; expressed as a fundamental boundary on royal prerogative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegal dispensing with laws by regal authority
rubrics_metrics.description: That the pretended power of dispensing with laws or the execution of laws by regal authority, as it hath been assumed and exercised of late, is illegal;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parliament prohibits the monarch from dispensing individuals from statutory obligations or enforcement absent parliamentary authority; distinguishes 'dispensing' from mere interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegality of ecclesiastical commissions/courts like the Court of Commissioners for Ecclesiastical Causes
rubrics_metrics.description: That the commission for erecting the late Court of Commissioners for Ecclesiastical Causes, and all other commissions and courts of like nature, are illegal and pernicious;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets special courts/commissions created by royal prerogative that bypass ordinary law; declared harmful and unlawful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Levying money for Crown without parliamentary grant is illegal
rubrics_metrics.description: That levying money for or to the use of the Crown by pretence of prerogative, without grant of Parliament, for longer time, or in other manner than the same is or shall be granted, is illegal;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms Parliament's exclusive role over taxation and Crown finances; prohibits unilateral raising of money by the Crown outside parliamentary grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to petition the king; prosecutions for petitioning illegal
rubrics_metrics.description: That it is the right of the subjects to petition the king, and all commitments and prosecutions for such petitioning are illegal;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes petitioning the monarch as a lawful right and forbids punishment or prosecution for exercising that right.

rubrics_metrics.name: No standing army in peacetime without Parliament's consent
rubrics_metrics.description: That the raising or keeping a standing army within the kingdom in time of peace, unless it be with consent of Parliament, is against law;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits the Crown's ability to maintain peacetime armed forces without parliamentary approval; a check on military power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of Protestant subjects to possess arms (as allowed by law)
rubrics_metrics.description: That the subjects which are Protestants may have arms for their defence suitable to their conditions and as allowed by law;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms a conditional right to bear arms for Protestants, subject to suitability and existing law; framed as a defensive liberty rather than an absolute individual right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free elections for members of Parliament
rubrics_metrics.description: That election of members of Parliament ought to be free;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declares the principle of free elections for parliamentary representatives as necessary to preserve liberties and legitimate government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parliamentary privilege: freedom of speech and proceedings protected
rubrics_metrics.description: That the freedom of speech and debates or proceedings in Parliament ought not to be impeached or questioned in any court or place out of Parliament;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes immunity for speech and proceedings in Parliament from external judicial or other questioning — foundational parliamentary privilege.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of excessive bail, fines, and cruel/unusual punishments
rubrics_metrics.description: That excessive bail ought not to be required, nor excessive fines imposed, nor cruel and unusual punishments inflicted;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets limits on pretrial security, financial penalties and corporal/cruel punishments; an early protection of humane criminal procedure and punishment standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury composition and selection rules (freeholders for high treason)
rubrics_metrics.description: That jurors ought to be duly impanelled and returned, and jurors which pass upon men in trials for high treason ought to be freeholders;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires proper jury selection and, for high treason trials, that jurors be freeholders (i.e., property holders), reflecting contemporary views on juror qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants/promises of fines and forfeitures before conviction are illegal and void
rubrics_metrics.description: That all grants and promises of fines and forfeitures of particular persons before conviction are illegal and void;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits pre-conviction commitments to fines or forfeitures targeted at specific persons; protects against punitive, anticipatory grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequent Parliaments for redress and preserving laws
rubrics_metrics.description: And that for redress of all grievances, and for the amending, strengthening and preserving of the laws, Parliaments ought to be held frequently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms the necessity of regular parliamentary sessions as a mechanism for legal reform, grievance redress and maintenance of liberty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement oaths of allegiance and supremacy (text provided)
rubrics_metrics.description: "I, A.B., do sincerely promise and swear that I will be faithful and bear true allegiance to their Majesties King William and Queen Mary..." and "I, A.B., do swear that I do from my heart abhor, detest and abjure... that princes excommunicated or deprived by the Pope ... may be deposed or murdered... And I do declare that no foreign prince, person, prelate, state or potentate hath or ought to have any jurisdiction, power, superiority, pre-eminence or authority, ecclesiastical or spiritual, within this realm."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the new oath texts to be taken in place of previous oaths of allegiance/supremacy; includes renunciations of papal authority and Catholic doctrines seen as threatening to the state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of William and Mary as sovereigns and limits on exercise of regal power
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolves that William and Mary be and be declared king and queen ... to hold the crown ... during their lives and the life of the survivor ... and that the sole and full exercise of the regal power be only in and executed by the said prince of Orange in the names of the said prince and princess during their joint lives...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parliament's settlement of the Crown on William and Mary, specifying joint reign arrangements and the form of exercise of regal authority during their joint lives and thereafter by heirs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of papists (Catholics) from succession and related disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: That all and every person and persons that is, are or shall be reconciled to or shall hold communion with the see or Church of Rome, or shall profess the popish religion, or shall marry a papist, shall be excluded and be for ever incapable to inherit, possess or enjoy the crown and government of this realm... and in all and every such case or cases the people of these realms shall be and are hereby absolved of their allegiance;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes a permanent incapacity on Catholics (and those marrying Catholics) to inherit or exercise the Crown; in such cases subjects are released from allegiance to that person and succession passes as if the Catholic were dead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that future monarchs make and repeat statutory declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: That every king and queen of this realm who at any time hereafter shall come to and succeed in the imperial crown ... shall on the first day of the meeting of the first Parliament next after his or her coming to the crown ... or at his or her coronation ... make, subscribe and audibly repeat the declaration mentioned in the statute made in the thirtieth year of the reign of King Charles the Second ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates that new monarchs publicly make and subscribe to a specified anti-papist declaration at first Parliament or coronation; includes a procedure if the monarch is under age twelve (declaration upon achieving twelve at next Parliament/coronation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on dispensation by non obstante except as provided
rubrics_metrics.description: And be it further declared and enacted ... that from and after this present session of Parliament no dispensation by non obstante of or to any statute or any part thereof shall be allowed, but that the same shall be held void and of no effect, except a dispensation be allowed of in such statute, and except in such cases as shall be specially provided for by one or more bill or bills to be passed during this present session of Parliament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declares that general 'non obstante' dispensations (clauses allowing deviation from statutes) cannot be used to override statutes going forward, except where the statute itself allows or where Parliament passes a specific bill in the present session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saving clause for charters, grants or pardons before 23 October 1689
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided that no charter or grant or pardon granted before the three and twentieth day of October in the year of our Lord one thousand six hundred eighty-nine shall be any ways impeached or invalidated by this Act, but that the same shall be and remain of the same force and effect in law ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects pre-existing charters, grants and pardons from being retroactively nullified by the Act; a preservation clause for past legal acts.
